text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Service streaming.generate exceeded latency SLOs in us-east-1. p95 and p99 spikes detected. auto-page triggered.

mira_oncall: ack. I’m on it — gathering p95/p99 numbers and tracing.

mira_oncall: current window (5m): p95=420ms (baseline ~110ms), p99=2.1s (baseline ~650ms). error rate normal, but many streaming stalls (clients see long gaps between tokens).

raj_infra: noticed a config rollout 02:18 UTC touching prefix-hash salt (service: cache-proxy) — rollout id prefixhash-regen-20260314. Could be correlated.

sam_prodeng: @mira any customer-facing symptoms? which routes affected?

mira_oncall: Affected primarily: /v1/stream and /v1/chat/stream. Traffic pattern: long prompt sequences and some high-concurrency internal tests amplified it. CS reports 3 customers opened tickets about partial responses. @cs_olivia can you paste customer IDs?

cs_olivia: customer IDs: cust-984, cust-1012, cust-2154. They reported token gaps and partial finishes. No data breach reported.

kevin_sre: quick telemetry dump:
```
# metrics snippet
prefix_cache_hit_ratio{route="stream"} 0.18
prefix_cache_misses_total 12487
backend_get_latency_p95 18ms
backend_cache_fetch_latency_p95 520ms
```

kevin_sre: prefix cache hit rate tanked (~18% for stream). Backend hit latencies okay, but cache fetches are high — suggests cache miss storm and/or inconsistent key hashing.

tess_ml: we deployed a prefix-hash salt change in the config map to improve namespace entropy. It was rolled out cluster-wide at ~02:18 UTC. I pushed the change to reduce collisions for new model variants.

mira_oncall: can we confirm KV namespace keys changed? Any TTL/eviction config modified?

raj_infra: TTLs unchanged. The salt change alters key fingerprints so most existing prefixes no longer match, causing a cold-cache wave. Combined with high-concurrency traffic -> heavy backend load and streaming stalls due to KV backend pacing.

mira_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) revert salt change (rollback rollout), 2) increase prefix cache TTL to allow warmup window (temp), 3) trigger controlled warmup (synthetic requests) to repopulate prefix cache, 4) add temporary routing to dedicated capacity for heavy customers if needed. Assigning: raj to rollback, tess to coordinate config, kevin to run warmup script, mira to coordinate comms + monitor.

raj_infra: rolling back prefixhash-regen-20260314 now. using: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/cache-proxy -n us-east-1 --to-revision=12`

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback:cache-proxy rev:12 by raj_infra at 02:44:03 UTC.

mira_oncall: monitoring hit_ratio and p95.

kevin_sre: starting warmup job (python loop hitting top prefixes) — snippet: 
```
import requests
for p in open('top_prefixes.txt'):
    requests.post('https://internal.warmup/stream', json={'prefix': p.strip()}, timeout=3)
```
Launched warmup pods with concurrency=50.

sam_prodeng: I'll queue up a targeted traffic reroute for cust-984 & cust-1012 if stalls persist. Need customer consent for reroute? @cs_olivia

cs_olivia: customers notified: cust-984 and cust-1012 told we are mitigating and offered reroute; cust-2154 opted to wait.

mira_oncall: rollback finished. deploy-bot shows success.

deploy-bot: rollback complete: cache-proxy rev:12 succeeded at 02:52:07 UTC.

kevin_sre: metrics post-rollback (next 5m):
```
prefix_cache_hit_ratio{route="stream"} 0.64
p95=130ms
p99=720ms
```

mira_oncall: great — p95 returned near baseline, p99 improved but still slightly elevated. Streaming stalls reduced substantially per traces.

tess_ml: follow-up: we need a safer rollout path for prefix-hash salt changes. We should gate by canary cohort and prepopulate new keys or run dual-hash resolution for a grace period.

raj_infra: agree. Immediate postmortem actions:
- add canary toggle for prefix-hash salt changes
- add prewarm job as part of rollout pipeline (generate top prefixes and pre-fill)
- instrument more fine-grained metric for key namespace divergence (hash-mismatch-rate)

kevin_sre: also propose an automated fallback in cache-proxy: on surge of misses, fallback to previous salt for X minutes. Low-effort and effective.

sam_prodeng: customer impact notes for postmortem: 3 customers reported stalls, no data loss, SLA blips for streaming p95/p99 for ~30 minutes. Potential revenue impact low but ops pain.

mira_oncall: handoff to night oncall @kevin_sre. Key open items for handover:
- confirm warmup job fully finished and no remaining cold shards (check prefix_cache_misses_total trending down)
- validate hot path token gaps resolved (traces)
- schedule postmortem with infra + ml + sRE + prod eng + cs
- action item owner assignment (see raj: canary toggle, tess: dual-hash plan, kevin: fallback logic)

kevin_sre: taking handoff. I will run a 1h follow-up check at 03:30 UTC and post updates.

mira_oncall: thanks all. Summary (for logs): 02:18 UTC prefix-hash salt rollout -> cold-cache wave -> prefix_cache_hit_ratio down to 18% -> streaming p95/p99 spike and token gaps -> rollback at 02:52 UTC -> hit ratio recovered to ~64% -> remaining p99 elevated -> warmup + monitoring -> incident closed to active monitoring.

cs_olivia: customers updated. No escalations pending.

mira_oncall: leaving notes in PagerDuty and tagging postmortem. If any night oncall sees anomalies, escalate to raj and tess.

kevin_sre: logged actions into ticket INF-3421 and assigned owners. Will kick off postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 PT.

mira_oncall: +1. Closing thread for now, will reopen if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
